cells.tense: What passes between you and the people near you comes out even
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: Write down one arrangement that already works — who puts in what, who gets what back — on a page you can walk away from.
cells.core:
You're at the far end of a stretch where you gave and took with the people near you, and it came out even. Whoever needed more got more, whoever put in got back, and the fairness held while you were in the middle of it. Release belongs here: you have stopped propping the arrangement up by your own hand.

What's left is keeping what you built from drifting loose. Pick one arrangement that already works — what each side puts in, what each side gets — and put it down on one page where you can see it. Then step back. Something written in its own shape keeps running when nobody is standing under it, and that's how the evenness survives a busy month.
cells.sheetLine: What you released still holds without you.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in even measure
cells.place: Where you set down what no longer serves

cells.tense: You're bracing at a settlement that hasn't finished happening yet
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: For one week, carry your own part of what is actually here and stop keeping the count of what you've handed over and what you're owed.
cells.core:
In your head the account is already closed — who gave what, who still owes, how it comes out. The exchange itself hasn't finished, and you're holding it from the far side, so nothing current can reach you. Keeping score has crowded out the passing back and forth it was supposed to shield, and the people on your ledger can feel the scale sitting there.

Loosen your hold on how it ends, for a week. Carry your own share of what is actually here, all of it, and stop reaching for the outcome. No checking anyone else's half, no keeping the tally current. What you release is the finished version you wrote in advance — and the exchange finishes at its own pace once your hands come off it.

cells.tense: You kept handing things over after the exchange had already closed
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Notice what you keep offering that stopped coming back, and let that particular offer end — no explanation owed to anyone.
cells.core:
You're still at the address of an exchange that ended. Time, attention, the small courtesies — they go out the way they did, and nothing returns through that door: no word, no matching move, no acknowledgment. It keeps running because the habit is old, but you have already left the room, and the room hasn't caught up.

Before anything new can reach you, sort what's worth handing over from what you're only repeating. When you find what stopped being received, cross it off and stop. That is a real release, small and checkable. What it opens — a little room, a little time — hold for a week without filling it.

cells.tense: The release is already underway, and it goes by another name
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: When some give-and-take sits wrong, skip the explanation and the quick repair. Keep what you noticed, let the other thing stand too, and wait before speaking.
cells.core:
You let exchanges close. You choose what to hand over and what to stop handing over, and you decide when something ends. If asked, you'd say fairness in your life simply turns up — that it works out, that people are decent. There's a hand on it, and the hand is yours; you just don't count it as yours.

Before you name what you're doing, hold what you know. Next time something in a give-and-take sits wrong, skip the explanation and skip the quick repair. Let both things keep standing a while. Knowing the choice was yours is the difference between being carried along by it and doing it on purpose.
